title: After your master's in Germany: stay or go?
description: The options after a master's degree in Germany: the 18-month job search permit, the routes to a work permit and permanent residence, and how to run a German job search.
html:
Finishing a master's degree in Germany puts you in a strong position. The country wants graduates of its universities to stay, and the immigration rules make that easy. The decision is yours; here is what each path involves.

Stay or return

Graduates who stay can apply for a residence permit for job search that runs for 18 months, during which any work is allowed. Once you have a job in your field, you switch to a skilled-worker permit or an EU Blue Card, and after two to four years you can apply for permanent residence. Graduates who return home take a German degree that is recognised worldwide and a network that often leads back to German companies abroad.

Further study

A PhD is a paid research position at most universities, which makes it a job as much as a degree. Application is usually direct to a professor or a structured programme, and the residence permit for research follows.

Finding a job

Start before graduation: German companies recruit months ahead, and the final semester is the best time to apply. Use your university's career service, which has employer contacts. Rewrite your CV in the German format. Target mid-sized companies as well as the famous names; they hire many graduates and compete less for them. Expect two to three interview rounds and a process of a few weeks.

Language

A master's in English does not require German, but the job market largely does. B2 opens most doors; many employers accept B1 with a commitment to improve. Use the final year to get there.

The paperwork after graduation

Apply for the job search permit before your student permit expires, keep your health insurance running through the transition, and make sure your bank account and address registration are current. The immigration office will ask for proof of funds for the search period, which is where your existing Blocked Account or bank statements come in.
